source_text: XIII. Ταῦτα οὖν μετὰ τοσούτου τάχους ἐγένετο, θᾶττον ἢ ἐλέγετο, τῶν ὄχλων παραχρῆμα συναγόντων ἔκ τε τῶν ἐργαστηρίων καὶ βαλανείων ξύλα καὶ φρύγανα, μάλιστα Ἰουδαίων προθύμως, ὡς ἔθος αὐτοῖς, εἰς ταῦτα ὑπουργούντων. Ὅτε δὲ ἡ πυρὰ ἡτοιμάσθη, ἀποθέμενος ἑαυτῷ πάντα τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ λύσας τὴν ζώνην, ἐπειρᾶτο καὶ ὑπολύειν ἑαυτόν, μὴ πρότερον τοῦτο ποιῶν διὰ τὸ ἀεὶ ἕκαστον τῶν πιστῶν σπουδάζειν, ὅστις τάχιον τοῦ χρωτὸς αὐτοῦ ἅψηται. Ἐν παντὶ γὰρ ἀγαθῆς ἕνεκεν πολιτείας καὶ πρὸ τῆς μαρτυρίας ἐκεκόσμητο. Εὐθέως οὖν αὐτῷ περιετίθετο τὰ πρὸς τὴν πυρὰν ἡρμοσμένα ὄργανα. Μελλόντων δὲ αὐτῶν καὶ προσηλοῦν εἶπεν· Ἄφετέ με οὕτως· ὁ γὰρ δοὺς ὑπομεῖναι τὸ πῦρ, δώσει καὶ χωρὶς τῆς ὑμετέρας ἐκ τῶν ἥλων ἀσφαλείας ἄσχυλτον ἐπιμεῖναι τῇ πυρᾷ.
thought_title: The pyre is built and Polycarp refuses the nails
orientation: After the crowd demands that Polycarp be burned alive, the narrator describes the gathering of wood and Polycarp stripping for the fire.
pass_a_gloss: These things then happened with so much speed, faster than it was said, with the crowds immediately gathering wood and brushwood both from the workshops and from the baths, with Jews especially eagerly serving for these things, as is custom for them. And when the pyre had been prepared, having laid aside for himself all the garments and having loosened the belt, he was trying also to remove his shoes himself, not doing this before because always each of the faithful was eager as to who might touch his flesh sooner. For in everything on account of good conduct even before the martyrdom he had been adorned. Immediately then the instruments fitted for the pyre were being placed around him. And as they were about also to nail him up he said: Leave me thus. For the one who gave to endure the fire will also give to remain unmutilated at the pyre without the security from nails that is yours.

lemmas.gloss: to loosen and take off footwear
unmutilated, not torn or dragged away

choices.why: brief glossary requires martyrdom for this root with this sense of suffering unto death
literal service work of carrying fuel, not neutral helping; keeps who does what
literal passive perfect keeps the honor as already given state before death
literal command to leave him as he is, without adding please or force of restraint

pass_b_english: It all happened in a moment, faster than words can tell. The crowd rushed at once to gather timber and dry sticks from the workshops and bathhouses, and the Jews in particular threw themselves eagerly into serving the work, as they customarily do.

When the pyre was ready, Polycarp stripped off all his clothes himself and unfastened his belt, and he even tried to remove his own sandals. He had never done this before, because each of the faithful always hurried to be the first to touch his body. In every way he had been adorned by his good life even before his martyrdom. They at once fitted the trappings of the pyre around him, and when they were about to nail him as well, Polycarp said, "Leave me as I am. The one who has given me strength to endure the fire will also give me strength to remain undisturbed on the pyre without the safeguard of your nails."
notes: form ἄσχυλτον is uncertain in sense here; glossed as unmutilated in the sense of remaining firm and intact at the pyre
